subject.title: [SECURITY] Privilege Escalation Vulnerability: docker Group Assignment Bypasses Hardening Measures

question: Which supported operating model should replace direct rootful Docker-daemon access for the OpenClaw account: rootless Docker, or a root-controlled service interface with narrowly scoped operations?
rationale: Both approaches change installation, service management, upgrade behavior, and the security boundary; source evidence establishes the risk but cannot choose the intended operational tradeoff.

options.title: Support rootless Docker
options.body: Run the OpenClaw workload against a rootless Docker daemon and remove the account from the host rootful Docker group.

options.title: Use a root-controlled service boundary
options.body: Keep rootful Docker host-managed but ensure the OpenClaw account cannot access its socket directly, exposing only the required lifecycle operations through a constrained service interface.

options.title: Retain current model with explicit acceptance
options.body: Document Docker-group membership as root-equivalent and accept the reduced host-isolation claim for installations using this mode.

recommendation.title: Support rootless Docker
recommendation.body: Run the OpenClaw workload against a rootless Docker daemon and remove the account from the host rootful Docker group.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only human participant in the supplied discussion to propose a concrete alternative deployment model; repository ownership evidence was otherwise unavailable in the read-only inspection environment.
